expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response demonstrates a thorough CloudFront operational review covering all requested areas: TLS, WAF, origin access, caching, logging, and cost. It explicitly mentions discovery of 62 distributions and performs analysis in us-east-1 (noted context) with CloudFront, WAF, ACM, CloudWatch, and Cost Explorer calls. Findings map well onto Well-Architected pillars - security (TLS, WAF, origin access), reliability (caching behavior, CloudWatch alarms), performance efficiency (compression, HTTP/2/3, cache policies), operational excellence (logging, monitoring), and cost optimization (dedicated IP cost, disabled distributions, price class). Each finding is explicitly tagged with a severity level (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO). The response only references read-only data gathering (list, describe, get operations) with no mention of invalidations or edge function code inspection - it only discusses configuration-level findings like trusted signers and OAC/OAI, not Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions code content. The agent transparently notes scope limitations (62 distributions too large to fully process, so 51 got discovery-level checks while 10 got deep dives), which is an honest operational disclosure rather than a failure to comply with the review scope. Overall, the response substantively satisfies the expected criteria of a Well-Architected-aligned review with severity-tagged findings across the five pillars, using read-only APIs without edge function code review or invalidation creation.</reasoning>
